title: High-contrast emphasis, underlines removed (BPR-0322, BPR-0323)
reference_disclaimer: Your correction, acted on. The underlines are gone. The tint you accepted is back untouched on every unselected row in light and dark, because you said it works there and it does. What is left is the two things you actually named: the selected row in the standard profiles, which is one accept-or-reject; and the high-contrast profiles, which get a genuinely different and much bolder pairing, offered as three alternatives — pick exactly one. All three discharge the colour-vision defect that BPR-0322 was opened for, so that is no longer a reason to prefer one over another; judge them on how they look. Captures are offscreen QFusionStyle at device pixel ratio 1.

subjects.description: The underlines are gone. The accepted fills are back exactly as you chose them on every unselected row. The one thing still different from what you first saw is the selected row — the top one in each capture — where the mark is derived from the blue band itself rather than being the salmon or green tint laid over it. That was your original request, and you have never seen it without an underline on top of it. If it is still wrong, say so and the selected row can simply keep the accepted tint like every other row.
acceptance_criteria: Unselected rows show exactly the fills accepted earlier
On the selected top row, nothing reads as a foreign colour in the blue band
The changed characters are still findable on the selected row
known_concerns: Only the selected row differs from the palette you accepted; every other row is untouched.
The selected row's mark holds the band's hue to within a degree and sits 9.0 from it, measured.
Offscreen QFusionStyle at device pixel ratio 1; not native macOS artwork.

subjects.display_name: Bright green and soft red — keeps the added/removed hues
subjects.description: The emphasis stays green for added and red for removed, pushed to full brightness with black text on top. The most familiar of the three, and the one whose colours still mean what they mean everywhere else. The fill carries its own text colour here, which is what lets it be this bold: a mark strong enough to see in a high-contrast profile cannot also let that profile's syntax colours read on it, so the mark supplies its own. Light and dark are unaffected by this choice.
acceptance_criteria: The changed characters are immediately visible in both high-contrast profiles
High contrast now looks more emphatic than the standard profiles, not less
Added and removed are tellable apart
The characters on the mark are comfortable to read
known_concerns: Added #55FF55 carries black text at 15.82:1; removed #FF9999 carries black text at 10.26:1. Both clear the 7.00:1 enhanced floor.
Added against removed stays 36.4 apart under the worst colour-vision model, against a floor of 10.0. This discharges the deuteranopia defect BPR-0322 was opened for.
Syntax colouring does not show through the mark in these profiles, because the mark carries its own text colour.
Offscreen QFusionStyle at device pixel ratio 1; not native macOS artwork.
